name: Buda
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Buda, TX 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Buda, TX: Budafest weekend with a lighted night parade, Buda Holiday Lights, Santa at Cabela's and a library holiday open house.
lede: Buda does Christmas as one big downtown weekend: Budafest fills Main Street, City Park and the Downtown Greenbelt with a carnival, a craft market and a lighted night parade, and Buda Holiday Lights keep Historic Stagecoach Park glowing for weeks after.
celebrates: Budafest is the heart of Christmas in Buda. The City of Buda runs the three day festival from the Buda Welcome Center on Main Street, with kids' activities and a carnival at Buda City Park, a craft and art market in the Downtown Greenbelt, and a night parade and fireworks along Main Street. After the festival, Buda Holiday Lights turn Historic Stagecoach Park at 880 Main Street into a holiday light display on Wednesday to Saturday nights in December. Buda Public Library adds a holiday open house with crafts and food, and the Cabela's store beside Interstate 35 sets up Santa's Wonderland with free photos with Santa through Christmas Eve.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Buda held the 45th Annual Budafest from Friday, December 5, to Sunday, December 7, based at the Buda Welcome Center at 303 Main Street. The city's calendar invited families downtown for three days of holiday cheer, with kids' activities and a carnival at Buda City Park, a craft and art market in the Downtown Greenbelt, and a dazzling night parade and fireworks show along Main Street. The lighted night parade rolled on Saturday evening.
facts: Buda began as a railroad town. On April 1, 1881, Cornelia Trimble gave land for a depot on the International-Great Northern Railroad, and the stop was first called Du Pre. Local folklore says the name came from settlers pleading, do, pray, give us a depot. The town became Buda in 1887, a name often traced to the Spanish word viuda, meaning widow, perhaps for two widows who cooked at the Carrington Hotel for hungry rail passengers. Buda incorporated in 1948, and Budafest reaches its 46th year in 2026.
trains: Buda grew up around a depot on the International-Great Northern Railroad, and for years it was a favorite meal stop for rail passengers. There is no Capital MetroRail service this far south; the Red Line runs from Downtown Austin north to Leander. For a real passenger train, Amtrak's Texas Eagle stops at the San Marcos station on South Guadalupe Street, the next town south of Kyle, and at the Austin station. For a holiday train ride, the Austin Steam Train Association runs vintage excursions from Cedar Park, north of Austin.
train_links: Vintage train rides from Cedar Park, including the Hill Country Flyer and the North Pole Flyer at Christmas.

kidfact: Buda was first called Du Pre, after a train depot. Some people say the new name came from the Spanish word for widow, because two widows cooked meals for hungry train passengers.
faq: Budafest is a three day festival in early December. In 2025 it ran from Friday, December 5, to Sunday, December 7, and the 2026 festival is the 46th. The City of Buda bases the event at the Buda Welcome Center, 303 Main Street, and posts schedules on the city calendar and the Budafest website.
What is there for kids at Budafest?

The city lists kids' activities and a carnival at Buda City Park, a craft and art market in the Downtown Greenbelt, and a night parade and fireworks along Main Street. Because the festival spreads across downtown, families can walk between the park, the market and the parade route without moving the car.
Where are the Buda Holiday Lights?

Buda Holiday Lights fill Historic Stagecoach Park at 880 Main Street. The city calendar lists the display in weekly blocks, from Wednesday to Saturday, during December, so check the calendar for the nights it is open before you go. The park is on Main Street, so the lights pair well with dinner downtown.
Is there a free Santa photo in Buda?

Cabela's says every family at its Santa's Wonderland gets a free 4x6 photo with Santa plus a shareable video, with optional paid packages. The Buda store sits beside Interstate 35 at 15570 South Interstate 35 Frontage Road, and Santa stays until Christmas Eve.
How did Buda get its name?

The railroad stop was first called Du Pre when Cornelia Trimble donated land for a depot in 1881. It became Buda in 1887. The Texas State Historical Association says the name is commonly traced to the Spanish word viuda, meaning widow, possibly for two widows who cooked at the Carrington Hotel.
